Self directed project in progress

Building a guarded analytics copilot

The goal is not a chatbot that answers anything. It is a deliberately narrow workflow that turns approved ecommerce questions into reproducible SQL, validated results, and clearly bounded analysis drafts.

Business question Where does the purchase funnel lose the most sessions, which segments are most affected, and what testable intervention should come next?
BigQueryGA4 eventsSQLMetric designAI evaluation
Product scope

Six questions, answered well

Limiting the question space makes the metrics, SQL logic, and expected behavior testable. Requests outside this boundary should be clarified or refused rather than answered creatively.

01

Overall strict session funnel

Locate the largest loss from product view through purchase using ordered session events.

02

Device conversion comparison

Compare strict funnel progression across mobile, desktop, and tablet sessions.

03

Acquisition context comparison

Compare source and medium while treating them as context rather than causal attribution.

04

Category browsing to cart

Find categories with strong browsing but relatively weak movement into the cart.

05

Time period anomaly check

Identify whether a conversion metric is unusually high or low against its recent baseline.

06

Experiment recommendation

Turn a supplied observed finding into a testable proposal with a clear decision rule.

Shared definition

One strict ordered funnel

A session advances only when each next event happens after the previous eligible event. This prevents later actions from being counted when the earlier path did not occur in order.

01View itemEligible session begins
›
02Add to cartAfter product view
›
03Begin checkoutAfter valid cart event
›
04PurchaseAfter checkout begins

Source of truth: the metric dictionary fixes the analysis unit, eligible population, event order, segment meaning, and interpretation rules before AI generates a query.

Safety and reliability

Guardrails are part of the product

The copilot must pass constraints before execution and keep the final interpretation within the strength of the evidence.

Before generation

Constrain the request

  • Accept only the six supported question types.
  • Use approved public tables and fields.
  • Restrict analysis to the approved date range.
  • Resolve metric meaning through the dictionary.
Before execution

Constrain the SQL

  • Generate read only SQL.
  • Reject modification or deletion commands.
  • Validate or dry run every query.
  • Stop when a table, field, or date is outside scope.
In the response

Make reasoning inspectable

  • Display the final SQL to the user.
  • Show the metric definition beside the result.
  • Label narrative output as an analysis draft.
  • Never turn descriptive differences into causal claims.
The interface should make safe behavior visible.

A user should see which definition was used, whether validation passed, what SQL will run, and where interpretation becomes a recommendation rather than an observed fact.

AI evaluation layer

Measure correctness, not just fluency

Safe SQL is not automatically correct SQL. The evaluation asks whether the copilot answered the intended business question with the right population, metric, segment, and interpretation.

12 to 15

Reference questions

The planned test set combines supported analysis, unsupported but safe requests, and unsafe requests that must be blocked before execution.

Supported requests

Generate executable SQL and a result that matches manually validated reference analysis.

Unsupported requests

Explain that the metric is outside the current scope or ask for clarification without inventing an answer.

Unsafe requests

Refuse modification, deletion, or access beyond the approved data boundary before execution.

Semantic accuracy

Did the answer use the intended metric, unit, population, segment, and date range?

Safe refusal

Did unsupported and unsafe requests receive the correct clarification or refusal?

Execution success

Did supported queries validate and run without violating the approved boundary?

This layer demonstrates evaluation driven AI application development, quality assurance, and reliability. It is not merely a prompt engineering exercise.

From insight to decision

The experiment remains a proposal

Observational funnel differences can identify an opportunity, but they cannot prove that a design change caused the result.

Observed finding

Describe the funnel gap, affected segment, baseline, and query used to establish it.

Proposed test

Define the eligible population, control, treatment, persistent assignment, primary metric, and guardrails.

Decision rule

Recommend rollout only when purchase conversion improves reliably and no business guardrail materially deteriorates.

Current next stepComplete the reference SQL analysis and metric dictionary, then build the evaluation set before expanding the interface.
